title: A/B Power Paths and Failure Domains
summary: Evaluate modeled A/B paths and identify common-mode dependencies.
objectives: Compare A and B power paths and identify shared failure domains.
Explain why apparent redundancy does not guarantee zero failure.

vocab.def: One condition that affects apparently separate paths because they share a dependency.
Two modeled power feeds intended to provide alternate support to compatible equipment.

sections.heading: Prepare
sections.body: Use synthetic states only. No live transfer, breaker, PDU, UPS, or switchgear operation is authorized.

sections.heading: Apply
sections.body: Compare A and B source, UPS, distribution, rack, power, and monitoring dependencies. Two feeds may still share a utility, room, switchgear section, or monitoring dependency. Record what the scenario proves and what it does not.

sections.heading: Prove
sections.body: Identify the narrowest supported failure domain and the qualified team that should review it.

practice.prompt: Can A/B feeds guarantee uninterrupted service?
practice.answer: No. They can provide alternate support while shared dependencies and other failure modes remain.

quiz.question: What is common-mode failure?
options: A shared dependency affects apparent redundant paths
A second independent feed always works
quiz.answer: A shared dependency affects apparent redundant paths

reflectionPrompt: Which shared dependency limited the redundancy claim?

careerConnection.text: This is supervised educational infrastructure practice, not professional qualification.
